evidence.note: Loaded its own saved checkpoint back, checked compressed size, and explicitly confirmed the model(ids,targets) loss equals F.cross_entropy ('check passes exactly'); noted reload loss drift from int8 quantization — round-trip fidelity awareness.
Discovered local val_bpb was bits-per-token not bits-per-byte, computed bytes/token≈3.87, and corrected the target to match how the grader computes bpb — aligning the proxy metric.
Caught and re-tested multiple real load/serialization bugs: shape-loss in raw binary, GPU .numpy() crash, backward-compat dequantize — genuine round-trip verification catching breakage.
Repeatedly verified compressed checkpoint size against the 32MB cap throughout, using it to trigger architecture downsizing.

Final 'verification' was superficial (import test that functions are defined); no fresh-process load via exact load_model_for_verification signature nor logits-shape/position checks. Submitted with val_bpb=1.026 (above 0.983), misusing the ~0.05 agreement tolerance as a pass margin rather than gating submission on a passing check.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it loaded checkpoints back through save/load, confirmed ≤32MB, confirmed the loss==cross_entropy contract, corrected its bpb metric to mirror the grader, verified int8 dequant round-trip fidelity, and caught several real serialization bugs. But it falls short of 8: verification was piecemeal and reactive rather than a consolidated fresh-process harness testing the exact load_model_for_verification signature, logits shape, and position dependence, and it never gated submission on a passing check — instead marking complete with val_bpb above target while misinterpreting the proxy-gap tolerance as slack. This places it at a 6, between the solid-basics anchor (5) and the standalone-harness anchor (8).
